content.text: {"headline":"Approve R1: maximum compliant overtime plus free levers. It is the best available plan, but it still falls short of the 80% target (73.8% predicted for 12:30–15:30).","why":"Two problems are hitting at once. The FD special-rate email (MKT-2026-556) has pushed general calls 20–45% over forecast, with new_offer_enquiry at 2.74x normal. Payments is about 4 agents short (35 vs 39) because of extra sick calls. If we do nothing, service level for 12:30–15:30 sits at 40.5%, with 15.6% of callers abandoning. R1 offers overtime to 35 general agents (13:00–15:00) and 10 more (15:00–16:00), plus 8 payments agents (13:00–15:00). It also adds 20% chat deflection of new_offer_enquiry, IVR callback on general, 30-minute break delays on both queues, and cancels the 15:30 general coaching. Predicted results are 73.8% overall (general 71.4%, payments 76.3%) and a 5.2% abandon rate. Rest of day recovers to 84.7%. No compliant option reaches 80%, and R1 gets closest.","trade_offs":["Cost: ₹12,495, the most expensive option. R2 costs ₹8,940 for 68.4% and P4 costs ₹7,140 for 60.7%. That is about ₹3,555 more than R2 for roughly 5 more points.","Both queues improve under R1, so neither is sacrificed for the other. Payments goes from 55.7% to 76.3% and general from 26.6% to 71.4%.","P2 and P3 use an IVR known-issue message, which breaks policy CX-01 because there is no confirmed outage. P3 would also only reach 68.3%.","No-cost levers alone (P1) barely help: 41.6% for ₹675."],"watch":"Overtime uptake is the main risk. The 73.8% assumes 53 agents accept the offers, so confirm acceptances quickly, especially the 35 general agents for 13:00. Track new_offer_enquiry volume against forecast in case the campaign response keeps growing. Also check that the payments sick-call gap doesn't widen."}
